tags.wreck_type: German cargo freighter (HAPAG Hamburg America Line)
tags.sinking_method: scuttled by crew (seacocks opened, fires set)
tags.note: Lies on port side, depth 5-18m. Broken in two amidships by 1953 storm. Largest wreck accessible to divers in Caribbean. Length/tonnage re-confirmed 2026-07-09 via Wikipedia (398.3ft/121.4m, 4,363 GRT), consistent with PADI, RushKult, Aruba.com. JADS Aruba's operator listing cites an outlier ~430ft/144m figure not corroborated elsewhere; retained 398ft/121m as the majority-sourced figure and flagged the discrepancy in the markdown.

Inner bowl 55ft/17m, outer reef slope to 90ft/27m. Kappel tugboat wreck (51ft/15m) sunk November 2009 on sandy bottom adjacent to reef. Shore entry. Re-checked 2026-07-09 against current jadsaruba.com listing (inner 55ft, outer 90ft, Kappel 45ft) — consistent, no changes.

Re-checked 2026-07-09: divers-guide.com now lists max depth 15m (previously recorded as 15-35ft/4-11m in prior pass — depth field corrected to match current source). Seagrass/sand areas transitioning to coral patches near shore, deeper reef further out. Calm bay, minimal current. Green sea turtles, grouper, schoolmaster snapper confirmed by divers-guide.com.

Scattered Lockheed Lodestar aircraft wreck at ~12m depth. Turtle feeding and cleaning station for green and hawksbill turtles. Re-checked 2026-07-09: jadsaruba.com confirms max 50ft/16m — depth field corrected from 11m to 16m to match the cited source (was internally inconsistent with the markdown body, which already cited 16m).

Only the midsection remains at 25ft/8m. Fore and aft sections were salvaged, joined, and rebuilt in Baltimore. Midsection used post-war as Dutch Navy target practice before becoming dive site. Re-confirmed 2026-07-09 via Wikipedia and willemsubmerged.wordpress.com: 355ft length, 4,317 GRT, built 1938, torpedoed by U-156 Feb 16 1942 as part of Operation Neuland — no discrepancies found.

Intentionally scuttled as artificial reef. Bow at 18m, propeller at 27m. Upright on sandy bottom. Previously named Blackthorn (1959), Rudyard (1976), Jane Sea (1980), then renamed Jane C. Cocaine story is contested - Aruba Ports Authority records indicate engine failure and abandonment. Re-confirmed 2026-07-09 via puredivingaruba.com and willemsubmerged.wordpress.com: 57m/190ft length, launched Dec 30 1959, scuttled Sept 4 1988 south of Barcadera — no discrepancies found.

Hard coral reef, max 75ft/25m per JADS. Schools of jacks, snapper, occasional barracuda. Southern coast with good visibility. Re-checked 2026-07-09: depth field corrected from 23m to 25m to match the cited jadsaruba.com figure (75ft/25m), which the markdown body already quoted.

Re-checked 2026-07-09: divers-guide.com now lists max depth 12m (depth field corrected from 5m, which reflected only the shallow inshore portion). Crystal clear calm water, shallow near shore. Brain and leaf coral, stingrays, turtles, starfish on sandy bottom. Good macro site. Training and certification dives. Visibility 25m.

Two aircraft: (1) Convair 240 - scattered by storms, wing tip 14m/46ft to cockpit 22m/72ft; (2) Air Aruba NAMC YS-11 - intact, upright, cockpit 16m/52ft to tail 27m/90ft. No Beech 18. YS-11 sunk 2004 by Aruba Water Sports Association. Location: in front of Renaissance Island. Re-checked 2026-07-09: puredivingaruba.com's per-aircraft depth breakdown (used above) is the most granular operator source and is retained. Conflicting secondary claims found: (a) JADS Aruba's 'Renaissance Airplanes' listing calls the smaller aircraft a 'Convair 340' (not 240) with a combined max depth of 85ft/26m; (b) scuba.com and other travel-blog sources describe the Convair as 'confiscated during a drug bust in the late 1980s' and give a different depth breakdown (45ft/80ft) attributed to Hurricane Lenny (1999) damage. Neither claim is corroborated by the primary dive-operator sources, so both are flagged as unconfirmed rather than stated as fact.

Reef slope transitioning to wall drop-off reaching ~100ft/33m per JADS. Hard and soft coral. Advanced due to depth potential. Re-checked 2026-07-09: depth field corrected from 30m to 33m to match the cited jadsaruba.com figure (100ft/33m), which the markdown body already quoted.

Depths 20-60ft. Enormous gorgonian sea fans, brain and star corals, brilliant purple/orange sponges. Barracuda common above reef top. Re-checked 2026-07-09: current jadsaruba.com listing does not name this site individually (only reachable via prior source snapshot); yellowcunucu.com and visitaruba.com content unchanged. No corrections needed.

Coral slope off De Palm Island, 15-120ft depth range. Cessna 414 wreck intentionally sunk as artificial reef. Moray eels, parrotfish, nurse sharks, great barracuda. Drift diving possible. 10 min by boat. Re-confirmed 2026-07-09 via duikersgids.nl: max 20m, nurse sharks/moray eels/parrotfish/purple tube sponges explicitly listed at this specific site — no discrepancies found.

tags.name: California
tags.wreck_type: British wooden steamship (West India and Pacific Steamship Company)
tags.note: North/windward coast. Depth 10-14m (30-45ft). Rarely dived - no regular dive operator schedule due to rough seas and strong currents. Little remains of original wooden structure. September-October offer best chance of calm conditions. Re-confirmed 2026-07-09 via ScubaBoard, divers-guide.com, and in-aruba.com: Sept 23 1891 wrecking date, one fatality (the engineer), max depth 14m — no discrepancies found.

tags.name: Antilla Shipwreck
tags.note: OSM polygon of the same SS Antilla wreck as the SS Antilla Wreck entry (curated). Coordinates differ slightly (OSM polygon centroid vs curated point). Both reference the same 398ft/121m German freighter scuttled May 10, 1940. Hull visible at low tide. Re-confirmed 2026-07-09 alongside SS Antilla Wreck entry — see that entry's note for the JADS length-discrepancy flag. This remains a duplicate record of the same physical site; flagged for future de-duplication but left in place as it predates this QA pass and de-duplication is out of scope here.
